subjects/physics/foundational/motion-1d: Ever watched a sprinter speed up off the blocks? This lesson tracks moving things on a straight line and shows you how to work out how fast something goes and how quickly it speeds up.
subjects/physics/foundational/newtons-la: Find out the three simple rules Isaac Newton wrote down over 300 years ago that still explain everything from a rolling marble to a rocket blasting off — like why you lurch forward when a bus stops.
subjects/physics/foundational/energy-con: Build your own roller coaster and watch energy swap between height and speed — speeding up on the drops, slowing on the climbs — without ever disappearing.
subjects/chemistry/foundational/atomic-s: Atoms are like tiny solar systems with a heavy core and electrons whizzing around. Add electrons one by one and build the first twenty elements, from plain hydrogen all the way to calcium.
subjects/chemistry/foundational/periodic: Discover the giant chart that lines up all 118 elements, and how a Russian scientist in 1869 spotted the pattern so well he could predict elements nobody had found yet.
subjects/biology/foundational/cell-struc: Explore the tiny rooms inside every living thing and meet each part's job — then watch one cell split perfectly in two to make a copy of itself.
subjects/biology/foundational/photosynth: Plants cook their own food using sunlight, and living things unlock that food for energy. See the two amazing recipes that run almost every food chain on Earth.
subjects/biology/foundational/dna-heredi: Why do you have your mum's eyes or your dad's curly hair? Follow DNA — the instruction manual inside you — from pea-plant experiments to the double helix and gene editing.
subjects/math/foundational/linear-functi: Drag two sliders and watch a straight line tilt and slide — that's all a linear function is, and you'll soon predict exactly where it goes.
subjects/math/foundational/quadratics: Throw a ball and its path traces a graceful U-shaped curve. Bend this curve yourself, find where it crosses zero, and read the secrets hiding inside the equation.
subjects/astronomy/foundational/orbits-a: Sweep a planet around its star and discover that orbits aren't perfect circles but stretched-out ovals — and that planets speed up whenever they swing close to the Sun.
subjects/astronomy/foundational/solar-sy: If the Sun were a football, Earth would be a tiny seed far down the street. Take a to-scale walk through the planets, all the way out to Voyager's slow journey into deep space.
subjects/earth-science/foundational/rock: Rocks never sit still — over millions of years they melt, crumble, squish and reform. Step through the endless loop that turns lava into sand and sand back into stone.
subjects/earth-science/foundational/eart: Dig 6,371 kilometres down (virtually!) through the rocky crust, the slowly flowing mantle and a sea of liquid metal, all the way to a solid iron ball at Earth's heart.
subjects/environmental-science/foundatio: Carbon is always on the move — through air, oceans, plants and you. See where humans add extra, and meet the famous graph that has watched it climb since 1958.
Follow the energy in a grassland: grass feeds grasshoppers, grasshoppers feed birds. Find out why each step wastes most of the energy — and why lions are always rarer than zebras.
subjects/history/foundational/cradles-of: Scrub through 3,000 years and watch the first cities grow — with walls, writing and kings — from ancient Uruk all the way to the fall of Rome.
subjects/history/foundational/medieval-w: Travel the thousand years between ancient Rome and the Renaissance: shining cathedrals, wise Islamic scholars, a terrible plague and a printing machine that changed everything.
subjects/geography/foundational/latitude: Why is it always icy at the poles and steamy at the equator? See how sunlight strikes our tilted planet differently at each latitude, creating every climate zone.
subjects/geography/foundational/plate-te: The ground under your feet is creeping a few centimetres every year! Learn how one scientist's mocked idea — drifting continents — turned out to explain earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains.
subjects/geography/foundational/ecosyste: From frozen Antarctic ice to steamy rainforests, discover how sunlight, water and temperature paint Earth with its great living zones — and what survives in each one.
subjects/economics/foundational/supply-a: Why do ice creams cost more on hot days? Play with buyers and sellers on a graph and watch the price settle where both sides are happy.
subjects/economics/foundational/money-in: Money is for swapping and saving — but when prices creep up year after year, your pocket money buys less. Find out why, and see history's wildest price explosion.
subjects/political-science/foundational/: Who gets to make the rules — one king, a small group, or everyone voting? Compare how countries are governed, from ancient Greece's famous list to today's democracies.
subjects/sociology/foundational/society-: You learn how to be you from the people around you. Explore how groups shape who we are — and the surprising experiments that showed how hard it is to disagree with a crowd.
subjects/psychology/foundational/memory: Where do your memories live? Meet the three stages your brain uses to store information, and watch the famous forgetting curve that shows how quickly new facts fade.
subjects/philosophy/foundational/logic-a: Learn to spot a good argument from a sneaky one. See how reasons build step by step to a conclusion, and uncover the classic tricks people use to fool you.
subjects/philosophy/foundational/ethics-: Is an action right because it helps people, because it follows a rule, or because it makes you a good person? Meet three big thinkers with three very different answers.
subjects/statistics/foundational/describ: Drag one extra-tall value into a data set and watch the average jump while the median barely budges. Find out which summary numbers you can really trust.
subjects/statistics/foundational/probabi: Flip coins and roll dice to see chance in action. Learn the rules for combining odds, and why casinos always win in the long run — it's maths, not luck.
subjects/computer-science/foundational/g: Some computer programs slog through a task while others race. Compare slow and speedy ways of sorting on one live graph and watch the gap explode as the job grows.
subjects/computer-science/foundational/b: Inside every computer, everything is ones and zeros. Learn to count like a machine and solve the puzzle of why one byte can never hold more than 255.
subjects/data-science/foundational/from-: A jumble of dots can hide a perfectly straight answer. Follow the six steps data scientists use to turn messy numbers into good decisions.
subjects/artificial-intelligence/foundat: How does a computer get better at a task? Watch a simple model learn by trial and error, rolling downhill step by step until it finds its best answer.
subjects/materials-science/foundational/: Why can you stretch rubber but not steel? Compare how different materials bend, stretch and snap, and see the curves that reveal what each one is good for.
subjects/agriculture/foundational/soil-w: A farm is one giant balancing act of soil, water and sunshine. Discover why a little extra fertiliser helps crops grow — but too much actually harms them.
subjects/neuroscience/foundational/the-n: Every thought you have is a tiny spark of electricity. Watch a brain cell charge up, fire its signal in a flash, then reset and wait for the next one.
subjects/anthropology/foundational/cultu: Travel 300,000 years back to meet our earliest ancestors, then follow humans as they spread across the whole planet and built thousands of different cultures.
subjects/law/foundational/what-makes-a-l: Where do laws actually come from — and who decides a court case? Uncover the layers of rules that keep society fair, from a country's constitution down to local regulations.
subjects/finance/foundational/compound-i: Money can grow money! Drag the interest rate and watch savings snowball bigger and bigger — and find out why ₹100 today beats ₹100 next year.
subjects/business/foundational/unit-econ: Can a lemonade stand actually make money? Move the price and cost sliders and find the exact moment when a business stops losing and starts earning.
subjects/religious-studies/foundational/: Take a respectful tour of the world's major religions — where each began, what its followers believe, and how scholars study beliefs with curious, open minds.
subjects/literature/foundational/how-to-: Every story ever told has a shape: a calm start, rising trouble, a big climax, then the wind-down. Plot your favourite tales and see the same skeleton in each one.
subjects/languages/foundational/how-to-l: Discover the method behind everyone who has ever learned a language: lots of listening and reading, the most useful words first, and revisiting each one just before you forget it.
subjects/engineering/foundational/static: Why doesn't a bridge squash or snap? See the invisible tug-of-war of forces inside every building — and the safety cushion engineers add so structures stay standing.
subjects/architecture/foundational/form-: Beams bend, arches push outward, and a hanging chain holds the secret shape of the strongest arches. Find out how clever builders let forces design the building.
subjects/visual-arts/foundational/value-: Every picture you have ever loved uses three secret dials: light and dark, colour, and where things sit. See how great artists cheat with all three to guide your eye.
subjects/art-history/foundational/walk-t: Stroll through 600 years of art in twelve famous works, from gold-backed medieval paintings to soup cans, and watch how artists' ways of seeing kept changing.
subjects/film/foundational/grammar-of-ci: Movies speak a language made of shots, cuts and clever editing. Learn to read it, starting with the very first films shown in 1895 — nothing but a train arriving!
subjects/design/foundational/design-is-d: Why do some apps just make sense while others leave you lost? Discover the design tricks — big, close and obvious — that guide your clicks before you even think.
subjects/journalism/foundational/verific: Before a news story goes to print, someone must check that it's true. Learn how reporters double-check their facts — and why the most important part comes first.
subjects/sports-science/foundational/tra: Exercise stresses your body, then rest makes it come back stronger. Meet the curve that shows why training too little does nothing — and too much can break you.
subjects/linguistics/foundational/how-la: How do simple mouth sounds turn into sentences full of meaning? Take language apart layer by layer, from single sounds to grammar, plus the story of how writing began.
subjects/music/foundational/sound-and-mu: Sound is just air wiggling — and music is wiggling with a pattern. Shape a real sound wave, hear how pitch works, and find out why an octave is simply doubling.
subjects/medicine/foundational/heart-cir: Your heart pushes about 7,300 litres of blood every single day! Follow one blood cell on its full journey — out to your toes, off to the lungs, and home again.
subjects/math/foundational/equations-and: An equation is a see-saw that must stay balanced — whatever you do to one side, you do to the other. Practise the moves that reveal the mystery number.
subjects/math/foundational/euclidean-geo: With just three starting rules and a compass, the ancient Greeks proved facts about triangles that are true everywhere, forever. Try your hand at building a proof.
subjects/math/foundational/perimeter-are: How much fence for a garden, how much grass fits inside it, how much water for the pool? Learn to measure lengths, flat spaces and full volumes.
subjects/math/foundational/ratios-percen: Half, double, 25% off, three parts sugar to one part flour — maths is brilliant at comparing things. Learn the tools that make any comparison easy.
subjects/chemistry/foundational/states-o: Ice, water, steam — same stuff, three forms! See how particles pack differently in solids, liquids and gases, and what temperature and pressure do to flip between them.
subjects/chemistry/foundational/mole-and: Chemists count atoms in giant batches called moles — one mole is 602,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 of something! Learn the counting trick that keeps every chemical recipe perfectly balanced.
subjects/chemistry/foundational/acids-ba: Lemon juice, soap and your stomach acid are all scored on the same pH scale, where each step is ten times stronger than the last. See where everyday things fall.
subjects/biology/foundational/classifica: Scientists have named millions of living things — how do they keep them straight? Learn the family tree of life and how to read its branching maps of who is related to whom.
subjects/biology/foundational/human-body: You are eleven teams in one: bones, blood, breathing, digestion and more, all working at once. Tour each body system and see how they pass the baton to each other.
subjects/biology/foundational/ecology-po: Watch a handful of rabbits multiply into thousands — then hit the wall of limited food. Explore how populations grow, compete and share out the living space in nature.
subjects/biology/foundational/evolution-: Darwin's big idea fits in four steps: offspring vary, some variations help, the helpful ones get passed on, and over time species change. See each step in action.
subjects/biology/foundational/movement-i: Watch tiny particles cross a cell's outer wall — spreading out on their own, water chasing balance, and doors the cell must pump open using energy.
subjects/biology/foundational/biological: Every living thing is built from four families of molecules: sugars for fuel, proteins for the work, fats for storage, and water making it all possible. Meet them all.
subjects/earth-science/foundational/mine: Salt, quartz and diamond are all minerals — atoms stacked like bricks in repeating patterns. Learn to spot the 4,000 named minerals by their crystal shapes and the neat ways they split.
subjects/earth-science/foundational/weat: Rain, rivers and glaciers are slow sculptors that have carved every valley and canyon you will ever see. Watch rock get worn down, carried away and dropped somewhere new.
subjects/earth-science/foundational/the-: The water in your glass once fell as rain, flowed down rivers and maybe hid underground for years — and it has been looping like this for billions of years.
subjects/earth-science/foundational/foss: Squeeze Earth's whole 4.54-billion-year story onto one ruler and you will see how tiny a slice humans take up. Learn to read fossils — the snapshot photos of ancient life.
subjects/philosophy/foundational/what-is: What makes anything real, right, or true? Meet the subject that asks the biggest questions of all, and learn how careful thinking — not just opinions — tries to answer them.
subjects/philosophy/foundational/epistem: How do you actually know something instead of just believing it? Explore what knowledge means, and the tricky puzzles that even caught the experts out.
subjects/philosophy/foundational/metaphy: Is the past still real, and could you have been someone else? Tackle the deep questions about what exists — objects, time, and what 'could have happened' even means.
subjects/philosophy/foundational/free-wi: If everything that happens has a cause, did you really choose your breakfast — or did the universe decide for you? Try out the famous arguments about free choice.
subjects/history/foundational/how-histor: Historians are detectives who solve mysteries using old letters, photos and objects. Learn to question every source, spot bias, and build an argument from solid evidence.
subjects/history/foundational/the-renais: A printing machine, a rediscovery of ancient ideas, and a monk with a list of complaints — see how three forces cracked medieval Europe wide open.
subjects/history/foundational/the-world-: Two world wars, thirty years, millions of lives — the biggest catastrophes in modern history remade the map and the rules. Follow how they began and what they left behind.
subjects/history/foundational/the-cold-w: For 44 years the world's two superpowers glared at each other without ever fighting head-on. See how spies, space races and proxy wars kept everyone holding their breath.
subjects/accounting/foundational/the-fun: Businesses keep score with numbers. Learn how recording every rupee shows whether a company is winning or losing, using one simple balancing rule: what you own equals what you owe.
subjects/drama/foundational/elements-of-: Step onto the stage and learn how actors build a scene — playing a character, timing their lines, and using space and tension to keep an audience gripped.
subjects/hospitality-tourism/foundationa: Over a billion trips are taken around the world each year. Find out why people travel, what makes a place worth visiting, and how tourism changes both travellers and destinations.
subjects/information-technology/foundati: Open up the box: the chips and parts are hardware, the instructions are software. Learn how computers work from the inside — and peek at tomorrow's tech like AI and virtual reality.
subjects/media-studies/foundational/the-: Every video, advert and headline is built four ways: how it speaks, who it shows, who made it, and who is watching. Learn to ask all four questions about anything on a screen.
subjects/criminology/foundational/changi: Some crimes never make the news because nobody reports them. Discover the crimes hiding in plain sight, why victims stay silent, and how crime statistics get counted.
subjects/public-health/foundational/prof: Doctors treat one sick person at a time; public health keeps whole cities well. See how clean water, vaccines and careful counting quietly save more lives than any single cure.
subjects/education/foundational/the-lear: Your brain is a learning machine — but some ways of studying work far better than others. Explore how learning really happens and how to become the boss of your own brain.
subjects/marketing/foundational/introduc: Why do you pick one drink over another? Marketing is the art of making something people genuinely value — and it starts by sizing up your rivals and yourself.
subjects/international-relations/foundat: Put on three different lenses — interests, deals and rulebooks — to understand why countries sometimes team up and sometimes squabble on the world stage.
subjects/biochemistry/foundational/prote: Your body builds thousands of tiny molecular machines from just twenty kinds of Lego bricks. See how the order of the bricks decides the shape, and the shape decides the job.
subjects/microbiology/foundational/the-m: There is a whole world of living things too small to see, and for most of history nobody knew it existed. Meet the microbes — and the microscopes that revealed them.
subjects/zoology/foundational/the-animal: What exactly makes an animal an animal? Compare body plans, from jellyfish to insects to you, and trace the moment single cells first joined together into teams.
subjects/botany/foundational/the-plant-c: Plant cells wear armour and run their own tiny solar panels. Look inside at the parts animals don't have — stiff walls, green chloroplasts and water balloons that keep plants upright.
subjects/marine-science/foundational/ear: The ocean covers most of our planet, and the Moon tugs its water up and down twice a day. Learn how the seas formed and how scientists divide them up.
subjects/meteorology/foundational/the-at: You live at the bottom of an ocean of air, stacked into layers with weather on the ground floor. See how sunshine powers it all, from gentle breezes to storms.
subjects/forensic-science/foundational/f: Every touch leaves a trace — that single idea powers all forensics. Discover how scientists turn fibres, fingerprints and specks of dirt into proof in a courtroom.
subjects/food-science/foundational/food-: Why does bread go stale but honey never spoils? Peek at the chemistry inside your food — its water, its molecules, and the reactions that make things tasty.
subjects/forestry/foundational/forests-a: A forest is more than a crowd of trees — it's a water filter, a wildlife home and a wood supply all at once. See how foresters keep those uses in balance.
subjects/nutrition-dietetics/foundationa: Food is fuel plus spare parts: big nutrients for energy and building, tiny ones for running the machinery. Learn what your body actually does with every bite.
subjects/chemical-engineering/foundation: Chemical engineers keep perfect ledgers — nothing enters or leaves without being counted. Learn to balance the materials and heat flowing through a factory like a maths detective.
subjects/civil-engineering/foundational/: Every bridge secretly does maths all day, pushing forces through its frame. Learn how engineers trace those forces — including what happens when a truck rolls across.
subjects/mechanical-engineering/foundati: How do you predict where a moving machine will go next? Master the engineer's toolkit — arrows for forces, laws for motion, and the rule that energy never appears from nowhere.
subjects/electrical-engineering/foundati: Electric current is like water in pipes, and circuits are the plumbing. Learn the two simple rules that let you work out every current and voltage in any circuit.
subjects/aerospace-engineering/foundatio: How does a 500-tonne jet stay in the sky? Watch air flow over a wing, see the pressure difference it creates, and meet the equation that turns it into lift.
subjects/biomedical-engineering/foundati: Look at your body the way an engineer does: a heart pump, kidney filters and nerve wires carrying signals. Once you see the systems, you can start designing fixes for them.
subjects/software-engineering/foundation: Before anyone writes a single line of code, someone must decide what to build. Learn how to gather wishes, write them as clear stories, and catch the requirements everyone forgets.
subjects/cybersecurity/foundational/secu: Keeping information safe means three things: only the right people can see it, nobody can secretly change it, and it is there when needed. Learn the language of security experts.
subjects/robotics/foundational/configura: A robot arm has joints, and every combination of joint angles is one exact pose. Learn to count a robot's freedoms and map out every position it could ever take.
subjects/game-development/foundational/g: Great games are made of simple loops: run, jump, collect, repeat. Learn how designers build the rules of fun — and how to test a whole game with just paper and pencil.
subjects/nursing/foundational/the-scienc: Behind every kind nurse is a scientist who knows the body, its invaders and its medicines. Get the science core that turns caring into healing.
subjects/pharmacy/foundational/pharmaceu: A pill is a cleverly designed molecule on a mission: find the right spot, do its job, then leave safely. Follow what a drug does — and what your body does right back.
subjects/dentistry/foundational/biomedic: Your mouth is an amazing machine of muscles, teeth and nerves. Take a detailed tour of the head and neck, and see the science a dentist needs before touching a tooth.
subjects/veterinary-medicine/foundationa: One medicine, many bodies: a dog, a parrot and a cow all work differently inside. Learn how vets compare animals' body systems and battle the germs that make them sick.
subjects/actuarial-science/foundational/: Someone has to put a fair price on risk — like what your car insurance should cost. Meet the maths toolkit of dice, distributions and averages that actuaries use.
subjects/social-work/foundational/the-so: Social workers step in when families and communities are struggling. Discover what the job really involves, where it came from, and the values that guide every tough decision.
subjects/counseling/foundational/the-cou: What does a counsellor actually do all day? Learn the rules and responsibilities — ethics, law and careful listening — behind the person who helps you untangle your feelings.
subjects/urban-planning/foundational/pla: Why is there a park here, shops there and roads between? Explore a century of big ideas about how cities should be arranged — and the famous failures that taught planners lessons.
subjects/archaeology/foundational/what-a: No time machine needed: archaeologists read history from the rubbish, tools and ruins people left behind. Learn how a broken pot or a stray bone can tell a whole story.
subjects/cognitive-science/foundational/: Is your brain like a computer? Cognitive science bets it can be studied that way, borrowing ideas from psychology, neuroscience and computing to work out how minds function.
subjects/classics/foundational/homer-and: Long before books, stories were memorised and sung. Meet the heroes of Greece's great epics — furious Achilles and cunning Odysseus — and learn how poems survived without paper.
subjects/creative-writing/foundational/c: Good writers don't just say it was scary — they show the creaking stair and the cold door handle. Practise choosing sharp details and shaping sentences that do exactly what you want.
subjects/dance/foundational/performance-: A dancer's whole body is their instrument. Learn how dancers train control and strength, express feelings through movement, and stay safe while doing it.
subjects/animation/foundational/the-twel: Cartoon characters feel alive because of twelve clever tricks, like squash-and-stretch and anticipation. Learn the rulebook Disney's artists wrote to fool your eye.
subjects/aviation/foundational/aircraft-: Before a plane ever leaves the ground, a pilot checks the engines, the dials and a long checklist. Step into the cockpit and learn what each instrument is saying.
subjects/culinary-arts/foundational/kitc: Chefs follow three golden rules: keep everything clean, handle knives with respect, and get organised before you cook. Learn the pro habits that make cooking safe and fun.
subjects/library-science/foundational/fo: A library isn't just books — it's a machine for organising everything people know. See how information is gathered, sorted and found again, and why that matters more than ever.
subjects/public-administration/foundatio: Who makes sure your rubbish gets collected and your water is clean? Meet the vast, quiet machinery of government workers that keeps everyday life running.
subjects/logistics-supply-chain/foundati: Your trainers travelled across oceans, warehouses and lorries before reaching your feet. Follow the journey products take, and learn the numbers companies use to keep it all moving.
subjects/gender-studies/foundational/sex: Words like 'sex' and 'gender' get mixed up all the time. Learn what each term really means and why careful words help researchers ask sharper questions about people's lives.
subjects/optometry/foundational/optics-f: Your glasses bend light so the world snaps into focus. Learn how light bends, what lenses and prisms do, and the tiny flaws that opticians must outsmart.
subjects/physiotherapy/foundational/the-: Every step, jump and throw is physics plus biology in action. Discover how movement experts study the body to help people recover from injuries and grow stronger.
subjects/occupational-therapy/foundation: In therapy, 'occupation' doesn't mean a job — it means everything you do, from brushing your teeth to playing football. Learn how therapists break any activity into its parts.
subjects/speech-therapy/foundational/spe: Speech is a team effort of tongue, lips and breath, turned into sound waves your ears decode. See how speech is made and heard — and what a hearing graph shows.
subjects/radiography/foundational/x-ray-: X-rays slip through your body but not through bone — that's how doctors photograph your skeleton. Learn how the images are made and the golden rule: keep the dose as low as possible.
subjects/paramedicine/foundational/ems-s: When you call an ambulance, a whole emergency system springs into action. Find out how paramedics are sent out, how crews stay safe, and the law they follow at the roadside.
subjects/medical-laboratory-science/foun: Before doctors can diagnose you, lab scientists handle your sample — carefully labelled, double-checked and kept safe. Go behind the scenes of the lab nobody sees.
subjects/environmental-engineering/found: What makes tap water safe to drink? Meet the chemistry and the tiny microbes that engineers must remove — plus the reactions they use to clean every drop.
subjects/industrial-engineering/foundati: Factories watch for trouble using special graphs that flag when a machine starts going wonky. Learn how statistics spots problems before any faulty product is made.
subjects/petroleum-engineering/foundatio: Oil hides in the tiny holes of deep underground rock, trapped between layers like water in a sponge. Learn how it formed and how engineers find it.
subjects/nuclear-engineering/foundationa: Radiation is invisible, but detectors can catch it particle by particle. Learn what radioactive decay really is, how radiation interacts with matter, and how we measure it.
subjects/operations-research/foundationa: How do you squeeze the most out of limited supplies — the best mix of products, routes or schedules? Learn to draw straight-line limits and find the best corner.
subjects/landscape-architecture/foundati: Before designers draw a single path or plant a single tree, they read the land: its slopes, soil, sun and views. Learn how great outdoor spaces get designed.
subjects/surveying/foundational/surveyin: How do builders measure huge distances with small tools? Use triangles, careful error-checking and even the curve of the Earth itself to measure the world.
subjects/communication-studies/foundatio: Sending a message is easy — getting the same meaning across is the hard part. Explore how thinkers explain communication, and why 'the medium is the message' still matters.
subjects/development-studies/foundationa: Is a country 'developed' just because it is rich? Compare ways of measuring how well people live — money, health, schooling — and see why poverty is more than a low income.
subjects/public-relations/foundational/w: PR is the craft of building trust between organisations and the public — not just flashy adverts. Learn what PR people do and how the job has quietly shaped history.
subjects/human-resources/foundational/hr: Behind every job is an agreement between worker and company, with rules to keep it fair. Learn what HR does and the legal floor no employer may go below.
subjects/real-estate/foundational/proper: When someone 'buys a house', what exactly do they own? Explore the surprising bundle of rights that comes with land — and what actually counts as yours.
subjects/photography/foundational/the-ex: A photo's brightness hangs on three dials: how wide the lens opens, how fast it blinks, and how sensitive the sensor is. Master the triangle and you master the camera.
subjects/fashion-design/foundational/fas: Every fashion collection starts as a scrapbook of ideas — colours, fabrics, photos and stories. Learn how designers research a theme and turn it into clothes.
subjects/interior-design/foundational/in: Why does one room feel calm while another feels cramped? Learn the designer's vocabulary — light, colour, layout — and follow a room from first brief to final plan.
subjects/illustration/foundational/drawi: Illustrators train their eyes as much as their hands. Practise really looking, composing a page, and finding your own style without losing the basics.
subjects/music-technology/foundational/r: How does a song get from a singer's voice to your headphones? Learn about microphones, where to place them, and the volume discipline that keeps recordings clean.
subjects/automotive-technology/foundatio: Mechanics work under two-tonne cars, so safety comes first. Learn how cars are lifted safely, how tools are used properly, and how to read the car's own manual.
subjects/welding/foundational/welding-sa: Welding joins metal with an arc as bright as the sun — and it brings dangerous light, fumes and sparks. Learn the safety gear and rules that make welding possible at all.
subjects/audiology/foundational/hearing-: Hearing starts as air pushing on your eardrum in tiny waves. Follow sound's journey into your ear and find out why some sounds seem loud while others hide.
subjects/respiratory-therapy/foundationa: How do therapists read a patient's breathing? Meet the numbers behind every breath — blood gases, scans and lung measurements — and what they say about the body.
subjects/radiation-therapy/foundational/: Some hospitals use a machine that fires carefully aimed energy beams to shrink tumours. Learn how a linear accelerator works and how doctors calculate the exact dose.
subjects/surgical-technology/foundationa: In an operating room, keeping germs out is a battle won with discipline. Learn how surgical teams sterilise tools, gown up, and guard a bubble of cleanliness around the patient.
subjects/dental-hygiene/foundational/the: Why do gums get sore and teeth decay? Dive into the science of your mouth — its parts, its tissues, and the germ battles happening along your gumline.
subjects/massage-therapy/foundational/bo: A massage therapist's hands need a mental map of the body. Learn the muscles and bones under the skin, plus the words experts use to describe movement.
subjects/plumbing/foundational/plumbing-: Clean water in, waste water out — plumbers make that magic happen. Meet the tools of the trade and the safety rules, especially for joining pipes with hot solder.
subjects/hvac/foundational/safety-and-th: Heating and cooling systems move heat around like a delivery service. Learn how heat travels, how to read the chart that describes air, and the safety rules of the trade.
subjects/electrical-trades/foundational/: Electricians follow two bibles: safety procedure and circuit theory. Learn why the rules matter, how circuits behave, and how a meter always tells the truth.
subjects/aviation-maintenance/foundation: Every plane flying today was signed off by a maintenance mechanic. Discover the drawings, physics and weight-and-balance maths behind the wrench — and the regulations that authorise it.
subjects/machining/foundational/measurem: Machinists shape metal to hair-thin precision, so their measuring tools are their most trusted friends. Learn to read a micrometer and why the metal's recipe decides the cut.
subjects/horticulture/foundational/knowi: Why does a cactus need so little water? Learn how plants are named, what roots, stems and leaves each do, and how a plant's shape tells you how to care for it.
subjects/special-education/foundational/: Every student learns differently, and the law promises schools will support those who need extra help. Learn about those legal promises and the personal plan made for each student.
subjects/translation-studies/foundationa: Translation isn't swapping words — it's carrying meaning across languages. See why a phrase can't always be said word-for-word, and how translators think before they write.
subjects/peace-conflict-studies/foundati: Peace is more than no war, and violence is more than fists — some harm is quiet and hidden. Learn the distinctions that help people study and build real peace.
subjects/emergency-management/foundation: Floods, fires and storms can't always be prevented, but their damage can. Follow the four-phase cycle: reduce risks before, get ready, respond during, and rebuild after.
